data.title: ‘Most bearish thing for XMR’ — What KuCoin’s Monero delisting means for liquidity
data.description:
KuCoin is in the news today after announcing that it would remove Monero [XMR] spot trading on 30th November. The exchange’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs accounted for over half of Monero’s spot trading volume on CoinGecko.

With such a large trading venue leaving, where would Monero traders go next?

When will KuCoin stop supporting XMR?

KuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC for 08:00 UTC on 30th November. Deposits have already been closed permanently too.

Withdrawals will close at 08:00 UTC on 31st December 2026. KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier over project-related issues, with the exchange also warning that stablecoin conversion of remaining balances won’t be guaranteed.

How concentrated was Monero trading?

At press time, CoinGecko highlighted $90.42 million in combined 24-hour volumes across KuCoin’s XMR/USDT and XMR/USDC pairs. Together, they accounted for 50.27% of Monero’s spot trading volume.

Including XMR/BTC and XMR/ETH, that brought KuCoin’s total to $104.60 million or 58.14%.

Hence, the question: Where could that trading move now? At the time of writing, the remaining exchanges showed more buy orders close to the market price, despite reporting a lower turnover.

Kraken’s XMR/USD pair had approximately $386,970 in buy orders within 2% below its price, compared to KuCoin’s XMR/USDT pair’s $85,683. WhiteBIT and HTX’s XMR/USDT pairs showed $260,810 and $196,231, respectively.

That gave Kraken roughly 4.5 times KuCoin’s nearby buying depth, with WhiteBIT and HTX also offering larger buy-side cushions. These orders could help absorb selling, although traders could cancel them at any time.

Could instant swaps lose an upstream supplier?

That access problem extended into services marketed as alternatives to CEXs.

X user and the founder of XMRHub called KuCoin’s delisting “the most bearish thing for $XMR.” According to the exec, the exchange supported swap services, liquidity, and onboarding.

Another X user, PerpetualCow, described the alleged connection more directly. He said,

Instant swap exchanges don’t have their own liquidity, they simply wrapped around Kucoin and sold/bought into their order books.

Still, the proposed dependency might explain why another exchange closure could affect apparently separate services. Swap interface routing orders through KuCoin would need another supplier, sufficient inventory, or a different execution route.

Dash’s Joel Valenzuela also raised a similar concern. He warned that further CEX losses could make no-KYC Monero swaps harder to obtain.

Finally, Cake Wallet founder Vik Sharma also directed users towards wallet-based swaps, writing,

Why does Monero keep getting delisted? Because it works!

Was regulation behind KuCoin’s decision?

The announcement followed another loss of exchange access earlier that month. MEXC ended XMR spot trading on 17th November. Its XMR Perpetual Futures closed separately on 13th November.

Kraken, for its part, had been explicit about its own rationale. It cited regulatory changes when halting XMR trading and deposits for European Economic Area customers on 31st October 2024.

Final Summary

  • KuCoin has scheduled the removal of XMR/USDT, XMR/USDC, XMR/ETH and XMR/BTC on 30th November.
  • Regulatory changes could have contributed to the exchange’s decision.

data.title: Bitcoin wallet privacy at risk? Researcher claims $0.35 attack could expose users’ IP addresses
data.description:
A potential privacy vulnerability in Bitcoin [BTC] could allow an attacker to link a Bitcoin wallet address to the IP address of the computer monitoring it. This, using a payment worth less than $0.35. For context, each planted transaction costs just $0.18 to $0.34, depending on the address format.

This vulnerability was identified by Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum. As it stands, although Bitcoin transactions are publicly recorded, wallet addresses are pseudonymous, meaning users can view transaction details without knowing who controls them.

Similarly, Bitcoin’s P2P network makes it difficult to link a wallet to a specific computer.

This is the reason why this revelation has raised an important question about Bitcoin’s privacy — Can someone identify the IP address associated with a Bitcoin wallet, even if the wallet owner never publicly reveals their identity?

Bitcoin wallet weakness comes to light

Well, according to researcher Sadeeq, the answer may be yes because of a weakness in how Bitcoin Core handles transaction rebroadcasting.

To understand the vulnerability, it is important to know how Bitcoin Core works. So, many users operate their own nodes, which maintain blockchain copies, validate transactions, and communicate with other nodes. These nodes can also run wallets that track Bitcoin addresses.

Each node has an IP address that can reveal its internet provider and approximate location. However, a wallet address does not normally expose the IP address of the computer tracking it. Hence, the vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

A loophole for attackers

According to the researcher, an attacker can exploit this by sending a small, low-fee payment to a targeted address. For this, the payment must meet Bitcoin’s minimum dust threshold while carrying a low enough fee to remain unconfirmed. Going forward, the attacker could then wait for the wallet to rebroadcast the planted transaction while monitoring different Bitcoin nodes.

When one node announces the transaction again, the attacker can identify it as the node whose wallet tracks the targeted address. This, in turn, would theoretically link the Bitcoin address to the node’s IP address, exposing information about its internet connection.

On the question of simulation involving five target wallets across six trials, Sadeeq successfully identified the correct wallet-tracking node in all 30 attempts. However, this does not necessarily reveal who owns the Bitcoin.

Therefore, even watch-only wallets, which monitor addresses without holding their private keys, can be affected. This also means that avoiding address reuse alone may not be enough to protect wallet privacy.

A potential solution?

Hence, as a potential workaround, users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting. However, this might lead to another problem, and that is that it stops automatic broadcasting of their own transactions. Therefore, proposed Bitcoin Core changes aim to address the issue, but they remain unreleased.

Here, it’s worth noting that these revelations coincided with the percentage of Bitcoin wallets currently at a loss entering a capitulation zone — historically associated with major market reversals. This could also mean that while retail investors panic, larger investors may be preparing to accumulate.

Final Summary

  • Vulnerability arises because Bitcoin Core may rebroadcast transactions that remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.
  • Users can disable automatic wallet broadcasting through the -walletbroadcast=0 setting.

data.title: NEAR Token price prediction — Why isn’t a 7% hike bullish enough for the altcoin?
data.description:
1alt HD: Here’s Why NEAR’s Higher-Timeframe Bullish Structure Holds Firm Despite 50% Drop From October Peak

NEAR Protocol’s [NEAR] token rallied by 7.4% in the last 24 hours, making it one of the biggest winners among the top-20 crypto assets by market capitalization. The altcoin’s daily trading volume hiked by nearly 45% too.

This boded well for the altcoin’s bulls, especially as NEAR reacted from the key $2.81-weekly support and rebounded higher.

As with most other altcoins, the question with NEAR is — Can the buyers convert the short-term momentum into something lasting? Or will the uncertainty around Bitcoin [BTC] and Ethereum [ETH] snuff out any bullish hopes for NEAR?

The bullish NEAR case

From August to October, NEAR rallied by 290%, from $1.53 to $6. Surging cross-chain swap volume on NEAR Intents, a cut in the maximum annual token issuance from 2.6% to 1.5%, and the confidential perpetual futures roll-out helped boost bullish sentiment.

The subsequent price rally was met with short liquidations, driving further gains.

After hitting its $6-high, the altcoin underwent a 50% correction and sunk to $3 once again.

Hence, it could be time to buy.

The 3-day timeframe’s price structure was bullish at press time. The altcoin’s price approached the 78.6% Fibonacci retracement level at $2.49, climbing to $3.04 at the time of writing.

Now, although the RSI was below neutral-50, the OBV has held up well in recent weeks’ selling. This may be a sign that after the 50% correction, buyers might be able to push the trend back in their favor.

Bitcoin’s weakness can affect NEAR’s fortunes

On the contrary, the 4-hour price structure was bearish. A trading session close above $3.28 is needed to flip the internal structure bullishly. A sustained move above $3.47 is required to confirm this timeframe’s bullish swing structure shift.

And yet, the first bullish sign has already occurred. The imbalance (white box) at $2.75 has been respected on the charts, kickstarting the gains made in the last 24 hours.

Given that this is a good start, bulls can keep an eye on NEAR token‘s progress. $3.47 will be the pivotal level that would signal a credible bullish trend shift.

Final Summary

  • NEAR Protocol’s token maintained its higher timeframe bullish bias despite going down just over 50% from the $6-high made in October.
  • Short-term momentum favored the buyers, but the $3.47-level needs to be overcome to present a credible bullish trend shift.

data.title: Why Hedera bears still have control despite HBAR’s 9% price surge
data.description:
Hedera [HBAR] has rallied 8.96% in 24 hours, alongside a modest 2.6% Bitcoin [BTC] bounce from its $57.3k low on Wednesday. Hedera’s token price bounce was one of the biggest among the top 35 crypto assets by market capitalization.

HBAR liquidity sweep could give rise to a move to the next magnetic zone

There was no direct catalyst or coin-specific development that helped Hedera post its heavy short-term gains. Rather, the price could be moving from one pocket of liquidity to another, aided by Bitcoin’s bounce.

The 2-week liquidation heatmap highlighted $0.0480-$0.0493 as a nearby cluster of long liquidations. The selling pressure saw HBAR decline from its $0.056 Monday peak.

After sweeping the $0.048 liquidity pocket, which was also around the $0.048 local low HBAR token made last week, the altcoin has rallied 11.3%.

This was a strong price reaction. CoinMarketCap data revealed a 26% daily trading volume increase, showing demand backed the short-term gains.

To the north, the $0.057 zone was a strong magnetic zone. A denser cluster of liquidity gathered around $0.06, the local supply zone. It appeared likely that HBAR was preparing to test these resistance zones.

HBAR traders should remember to book profits on the way up

While the short-term momentum and sizeable bullish relative strength against Bitcoin were tempting, buyers should remain cautious. The price trend on the 1-day timeframe was bearish.

In particular, the magnetic zones highlighted earlier at $0.057 and $0.06 were close to the local swing points from earlier this month, at $0.0548 and $0.0594.

It is highly likely that an HBAR foray into these zones would result in a setback as underwater and short-term holders rush to exit their positions.

The OBV was in a deep downtrend and revealed steady selling pressure in recent weeks. A pause in this downtrend would be a good sign for investors looking to buy.

Until $0.059 is breached and the OBV begins to reverse, swing traders and investors can maintain a bearish bias.

Final Summary

  • Hedera saw one of the biggest price gains in the past 24 hours among the top 35 crypto assets.
  • This show of short-term relative bullish strength must not distract swing traders from the altcoin’s longer-term downtrend.

data.title: Top 6 Solana APIs of November 2026
data.description:
Solana is an important blockchain network in the crypto space, famously known for its low transaction costs, fast processing capabilities, and high transaction throughput. APIs or Application Programming Interfaces, are rules that let 2 different softwares to interact with each other.

APIs on Solana help developers integrate blockchain functionality into their applications without having to operate or maintain their own RPC infrastructure or validator. Different APIs focus on different needs and factors, so for users it’s best to choose one that fits their needs depending on the data and performance. Here are our top picks for the best Solana APIs of the month:

1. Alchemy

Alchemy is a holistic platform with a wide range of options available for developers. It has JSON-RPC nodes, DAS APIs, and gRPC streaming. The broader developer platform is helpful for developers and teams alike with monitoring capabilities and development tooling options.

It also has a developer-focused space, which makes it convenient for everyone who wants to manage different blockchain integrations within a broader development ecosystem. Alchemy proves to be a good option for startups and developers who are building with multi-chain applications.

2. Helius 

Helius simplifies the process of interpreting and organizing large amounts of raw blockchain information that developers need to go through with its enhanced APIs. The DAS API lets applications retrieve information about digital assets like tokens and NFTs.

The platform also offers webhooks that are useful for applications to keep track of wallet activity. Helius’s broader infrastructure also offers Solana RPC access, historical transaction data, and real-time streaming through LaserStream.

3. QuickNode

QuickNode’s Solana API supports JSON-RPC API and provides low-latency, Yellowstone-compatible streaming on Mainnet and Devnet. It is built to scale dApps on the Solana blockchain.

Developers can submit transactions, interact with smart contracts, build apps, and read blockchain data. It is especially a great option for developers who are building multi-chain dApps, DeFi platforms, and other enterprise blockchain solutions.

4. Triton API

Triton’s API has been designed to help developers build reliable and scalable apps on Solana. It gives them access to the Solana blockchain data with its high-performance RPC endpoints and real-time data streaming services. The infrastructure also supports standard Solana RPC requests, Yellowstone gRPC streaming, and WebSocket subscriptions.

Triton is one of Solana’s original validators and has provided RPC since 2021. Devnet and testnet are provided to developers with every subscription, and JSON-RPC methods are used for reading accounts and tokens.

5. Dune API

Dune API is also useful for developers and helps them retrieve, investigate, and analyze Solana transactions, wallet activity, and on-chain events. It translates raw blockchain data into structured information.

The Execution API on Dune is great for complex historical analysis, aggregated metrics, and querying specific Solana programs. The platform also provides interactive dashboards, real-time data access and analytics for Web3 research.

6. Chainstack API

Chainstack helps developers build, scale and deploy dApps without having to manage complex blockchain nodes. Developers can connect apps to Solana through RPC endpoints and receive real-time blockchain notifications and account updates.

Users can also connect apps with standard Solana JSON-RPC methods and provide developer-friendly integrations and have blockchain data access.

Final word

APIs on Solana help to make blockchain developments easier and more efficient. Developers can improve the scalability of their projects and access real-time blockchain data. They bridge the gap between blockchain infrastructure and real-world applications and allow developers to focus on making innovative product rather than spending extra time managing data processing.

Users need to use their own discretion and research before making a desicion.

data.title: A $14.5M Lemon deal and a new D3 vault — What is Tether doing?
data.description:
Stablecoin giant Tether [USDT] has been making some moves lately. Here’s the rundown.

A $14.5M investment into Lemon, but…

… only $5M buys equity.

Tether has backed Argentine fintech app Lemon, with the former not putting a number on it when it announced the deal. Lemon did, however, saying that the package is worth $14.5 million.

Is there a catch? Yes.

According to Lemon CEO Marcelo Cavazzoli, only $5 million of that is an actual investment in the company’s shares. The other $9.5 million is an incentive plan linked to products the two will build together.

There’s a lot that’s unclear right now though. Neither side has shared Lemon’s valuation or how big a stake Tether is getting. There’s also no word on how or when the $9.5 million gets paid out. Tether is after more users for USDT and Tether Gold [XAUT] across Latin America. Lemon gives it a decent shot at that. The app is said to have 4.5 million verified users, and its main balance runs on USDT.

Worth noting, however, that Lemon’s not the only home for Tether this month.

USDT on D3’s domain platform through a Sentora-run vault

On the 9th, D3 launched a USD vault for Tether’s stablecoin. Users can deposit USDT, keep an eye on their position, and withdraw without leaving the platform.

Sentora built the system using its Earn OS and Upshift tools, which decide where deposited funds go. Money moves with the market, within a set of risk rules. It is said that the setup has already handled more than $2 billion.

But why a vault?

Domain buyers usually come in, make a deal, and leave. Earning on stablecoins gives them a reason to keep their money on the platform.

Just don’t mistake automated for guaranteed. Returns depend on the lending markets the vault uses. So, users are still trusting a whole stack of infrastructure with their dollars.

Final Summary

  • Tether has backed Lemon with $14.5M, but only $5M is equity.
  • USDT is now on D3 through a Sentora-run yield vault.

data.title: Fidelity files for Spot Chainlink ETF as LINK climbs 5.5% – Details
data.description:
In a recent turn of events, Fidelity Investments filed a Form S-1 registration statement with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to launch a spot Chainlink [LINK] exchange-traded product (ETP). 

All about Fidelity’s S-1 registration

According to the 25th November filing, the proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK. That said, the fund would also hold LINK tokens directly. This allows investors to gain exposure to LINK through traditional stock market accounts without having to purchase or manage the tokens themselves.

At the same time, the fund aims to track the Fidelity Chainlink Reference Rate, which calculates LINK’s price using a volume-weighted median methodology based on data from eligible spot markets.

 Notably, its holdings would be managed by three proposed custodians, including Anchorage Digital Bank, BitGo Bank & Trust, and Coinbase Custody Trust Company.

LINK’s price action and ETF analysis

As expected, this news did have a positive impact on LINK’s price, which was trading at $9.16 at press time after a hike of 5.5% in the past 24 hours. With this, Fidelity becomes the third asset manager to launch a LINK ETF besides Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK.

In fact, according to SoSo Value data, GLNK and CLNK have already recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively. This in turn has brought their combined cumulative inflows to approximately $176 million. However, neither fund recorded any new flows on the 25th of November, with both showing $0 in daily net inflows. 

How did other ETFs perform? 

This news comes as the broader cryptocurrency investment products recorded widespread outflows across major digital assets in the month of November. Starting with Bitcoin [BTC] ETFs, which witnessed the largest withdrawals, worth approximately $5.39 billion in net outflows, facing their worst month since launch.

Ethereum [ETH] ETFs too saw $1.30 billion worth of outflows. This was followed by XRP ETFs, which saw $29.18 million in outflows, while Solana [SOL] ETFs registered withdrawals of $57 million. Meanwhile, Dogecoin [DOGE] ETFs recorded relatively smaller outflows of $409,130.

Interestingly, not all products experienced negative flows, as HBAR ETFs attracted approximately $1.71 million in net inflows. This made it the only asset in the sea of ETFs to record positive flows on the day.

Final Summary

  • The proposed fund is expected to trade on Nasdaq under the provisional ticker FLNK.
  • Grayscale’s GLNK and Bitwise’s CLNK recorded cumulative net inflows of $128.12 million and $47.88 million, respectively.

data.title: XRP price eyes $1 – But THESE signals warn traders to stay cautious
data.description:
Ripple [XRP] was up 3.46% in the past 24 hours, with a daily trading volume uptick of 34%. The price bounce followed a Bitcoin [BTC] move back above $61k, which was likely a result of a short squeeze.

This price bounce was reflected across the altcoin market, which has gained 1.72% in its cumulative market cap in a day, reaching $2.07 trillion at the time of writing.

XRP was about to test the $1 resistance zone, a place it had faced rejection from earlier this week. Can the bulls succeed in reclaiming it as support this time?

Is the consolidation phase underway for XRP?

In September and October, XRP was oscillating between the $1.30 support zone and the $1.50-$1.55 supply zone. This consolidation gave way to a downtrend that reached a low below $0.90.

Over the past two weeks, the $0.893 and $1.00 levels have emerged as key levels on the daily timeframe for swing traders. A daily session close outside these boundaries will likely decide the direction of the next swing price move.

At press time, the CMF was at -0.12, signaling heavy selling pressure and capital outflows. The MACD was also moving below the zero line, a sign that downward momentum was prevalent. The MACD line made a bullish crossover above the signal line, an indication of short-term bounce potential.

Despite encouraging ETF flows over the past year, the altcoin’s performance had been lacklustre.

The trend was now firmly bearish, the Directional Movement Index asserted. This indicator’s -DI and ADX readings above 20 confirmed the downtrend, alongside the price structure.

Should XRP traders stay in the range?

Like the 1-day chart showed a sweep above $1 on Monday, XRP recently made a sweep of the $0.961 local peak in recent hours. Despite the short-term upward momentum, there is a chance of a pullback.

Potential buyers can wait to see the price reaction from the $0.92 and $0.86-$0.88 demand zones.

A bullish reaction on the hourly chart, in the form of something like an engulfing candle, would be a sign that bulls were ready to drive a move toward $1.00.

Traders should be wary of short-term volatility and wait for a positive reaction before buying. Risk-averse traders can remain sidelined until the higher timeframe trend gives a new direction with a move beyond $1.00 or $0.893.

Final Summary

  • XRP was one of the top altcoins with a sizeable price bounce in the past 24 hours.
  • Bulls were readying to make a move toward $1.00, but might face a correction toward $0.88 or $0.92 in the short term.

data.title: U.S. moves Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bill forward with a 20-year lockup plan
data.description:
The U.S. House Financial Services Committee has advanced H.R. 8957, known as the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, bringing the proposed legislation one step closer to a full House vote.

Introduced on the 21st of May 2026 by Republican Representative Nick Begich of Alaska, alongside Democratic Representative Jared Golden, the bill seeks to give the U.S. government’s Strategic Bitcoin [BTC] Reserve a formal legal foundation.

It proposes that the U.S. Treasury Department establish two separate structures within 180 days of the legislation becoming law. This includes a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve exclusively for Bitcoin and a Digital Asset Stockpile for other cryptocurrencies held by the federal government.

Details of the 20-year lockup plan

Under the proposal, Bitcoin owned by the federal government through criminal or civil asset forfeitures and other qualifying sources would be transferred to the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.

Here, the most significant provision is a 20-year minimum holding requirement, which would prevent the government from selling, swapping, auctioning, or using reserve Bitcoin as collateral during that period. At the same time, the bill also allows the Treasury Department to explore budget-neutral ways of acquiring additional Bitcoin without increasing the national debt.

Separately, the legislation proposes a Digital Asset Stockpile to manage other cryptocurrencies held by the federal government. Lastly, it also introduces requirements for transparency, auditing, and congressional reporting to ensure proper oversight of these assets.

Why does this matter?

The bill is particularly significant because it seeks to give the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve a statutory foundation. For its part, President Donald Trump had already established the reserve through an executive order in March 2025.

However, H.R. 8957 aims to formalize its structure and introduce additional safeguards, including the proposed 20-year holding period.

As of now, twenty months have already passed, and the U.S. government reportedly holds around 328,000 BTC, largely from seizures and forfeitures, while governments globally hold about 435,000 BTC.

Henceforth, if H.R. 8957 becomes law, the reserve would receive statutory backing, making it more difficult for a future administration to reverse the policy unilaterally.

Steps taken so far

The bill received approval from the House Financial Services Committee on 16th September 2026 in a 28-21 vote, with all Republican members voting in favor and all Democratic members opposing it.

Then, on the 24th of November, the committee formally reported the revised legislation to the full House, placing it on the Union Calendar and making it eligible for a floor vote. However, its chances of becoming law remain uncertain.

This is because the 119th Congress ends on the 3rd of January 2027, leaving limited time for the bill to pass the House, clear the Senate, and receive presidential approval.

Adding to this, market expectations also remain pessimistic, with Polymarket traders assigning only a 4% probability to the U.S. establishing a national Bitcoin reserve through legislation before 2027.

All of this coincided with Bitcoin trading at $60,355.92 at press time after a hike of 2.1% in the past 24 hours.

Final Summary

  • Bitcoin owned by the federal government through forfeitures would be transferred to the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve.
  • The chances of the bill becoming law remain uncertain as the 119th Congress ends on 3rd January 2027.

data.title: Bitcoin miners lose hashrate as hackers hijack up to 1,600 sites
data.description:
On the 25th of November, Bitcoin mining company Braiins warned that attackers had hijacked Bitcoin miners’ work through unencrypted pool connections.

Machines kept running while someone else received credit. That basically left operators paying electricity bills for work credited elsewhere.

Its investigation documented four episodes on the 20th of November, mostly in Europe. Each affected 1,050–1,600 mining sites and diverted 0.6–1.9 EH/s for six to 49 minutes.

Attackers forged internet routing announcements, known as BGP hijacking, to intercept connections and impersonate the pool. Miners reconnected to the same address, making the switch difficult to spot.

Earlier episodes hit Latin America between the 7th and 12th of November.

Responding to an X user, Braiins said the attacks exploited a weakness in Stratum V1, the protocol connecting miners to pools. Stratum V2 contributor Pavlenex added,

This is an attack on MINERS and their infrastructure and is not a vulnerability in Braiins Pool.

Did earlier warnings lead to upgrades?

The exposed protocol dates back to 2012, and warnings have been issued for years.

Braiins had flagged hashrate theft on the 18th of April 2020. It argued that preventing stolen revenue and reducing operating expenses would encourage upgrades more effectively than decentralization alone.

That history prompted Turtlecute, who works in product marketing at Braiins, to write,

For 14 years, we ignored SV1 issues.

When an X user asked whether this was the first publicly confirmed case, Pavlenex recalled earlier reports of interception attacks.

By November, the financial incentive for upgrading had become harder to dismiss. Braiins reported that miners’ machines showed normal activity while their pool dashboards recorded no credited hashrate.

How far had upgrades actually progressed?

Six months earlier, seven mining organizations had joined the Stratum V2 Working Group. These included ANTPOOL, Foundry, F2Pool, SpiderPool, Block, MARA Foundation, and DMND.

Reportedly, the organizations represented roughly 75% of the global hashrate at the time. Their backing gave the encrypted replacement substantial reach, but deployment remained uneven.

As of the 26th of November, the official directory listed Braiins Pool and DMND as production pools. It separately listed several solo pools and MARA Foundation’s industrial solo operation.

Foundry remained marked as work in progress, despite reported testing in November. ANTPOOL, F2Pool, and SpiderPool were absent from the production listings.

The exposure extended beyond V2 adoption. Braiins said most major pools’ public endpoints still offered only unencrypted Stratum V1 during its checks on the 23rd of November.

Braiins CEO Eli Nagar urged,

Pools, Miners, fix your URLs today

V2 encrypts mining traffic and verifies the pool’s identity, preventing an impersonator from receiving miners’ work. The November attacks showed the revenue consequences when industry support had yet to reach those connections.

Final Summary

  • Braiins reported Bitcoin hashrate hijacking across 1,000-plus mining sites.
  • Unencrypted connections and backups could redirect work while machines appeared healthy.
